chunks: Aban narrated from Salamah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh, from his father, peace be upon them:

That ʿAlī, peace be upon him, clothed the people in Iraq, and among the clothing there was a fine robe. Al-Ḥusayn, peace be upon him, asked him for it, but he refused. Then al-Ḥusayn, peace be upon him, said: “I will give you two robes in its place,” but he refused. He kept offering him more until it reached five, so he took them from him, then gave him the robe and placed the robes in his lap, saying: “I shall indeed take five for one.”

key_terms.الْعِرَاقِ: Iraq, the place where this event occurred
key_terms.الْكِسْوَةِ: the clothing or garments being distributed
key_terms.حَجْرِهِ: his lap, where the garments were placed
key_terms.خَمْساً: five, referring to the number of robes offered

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith show about exchanging one garment for multiple garments in Shia legal tradition?
ai.summary: This narration recounts an exchange between Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام and Imam al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام involving a fine robe and multiple robes offered in return. In the context of the chapter on usury, it serves as a report relevant to the discussion of exchanging garments in unequal quantities.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4011 - Aban narrated from Salamah, from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) from his father, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) that:

Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) distributed clothing among the people in Iraq, and among the garments was a fine robe. Imam Hussain ibn Ali (as) asked him for it, but Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) refused.
Imam Hussain ibn Ali (as) then said: "I will give you two robes in exchange for it."
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) refused.
Imam Hussain ibn Ali (as) continued offering until he reached five robes. Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) then took the robes from him, gave him the fine robe, and placed the robes in his lap, saying: "I will take five in exchange for one."
